questions.prompt: The ChatGPT docs say what about your first message in a chat?

options.text: It is only a starting point, and you can improve the result with follow-ups.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say: "Your first prompt is only a starting point". You can add context or ask for changes later.

options.text: It must be perfect, because the app can't change its answer after that.
options.explanation: The docs say the opposite: you don't need a perfect first prompt, and you can ask for changes.

options.text: It should be as short as possible, like a search, so the app can guess.
options.explanation: The docs ask you to state the goal, add the details that change the answer and describe the format.

questions.prompt: What do the Gemini Apps Help and the Claude Help Center both say about answers?

options.text: They are always correct when the app sounds very sure.
options.explanation: Both say answers can be wrong, even when they look convincing.

options.text: They can be wrong, so you check them before you use them.
options.explanation: Right. The Gemini help says "Gemini Apps can make mistakes" and to double-check responses. The Claude Help Center says answers can look correct but be very mistaken.

options.text: They are only wrong when you use a free plan of the app.
options.explanation: Neither page says this. Any answer can be wrong, on any plan.

questions.prompt: The Claude Help Center calls the context window "Claude's working memory". What does it say you can do when you hit its length limit?

options.text: Wait a few hours, and the old chat will grow bigger.
options.explanation: Waiting resets a usage limit, not the size of one chat.

options.text: Delete your account and sign up again.
options.explanation: Not needed. A new chat is enough.
Right. The page says that if you hit a length limit, "you can start a new conversation".
